newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - FTSE options busy in volatility trades.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FTSE options busy in volatility trades.

text.p: A sharp jump in the FTSE 100 index on Wednesday directed most of the activity in UK equity option towards index options rather than stock options, dealers said.
The main trades were volatility related in which an options position is hedged by an opposite trade in FTSE futures so that a profit can be made from changes in stock market volatility.
By 1505 GMT, the FTSE was up 28.0 at 4298.7 and June futures were up 28 points at 4321.
One trader, believing volatility will decline over coming months, sold straddles in European style FTSE against futures.
The deal involved selling 1,000 September 4325 puts and calls at prices around 155p and 184p respectively against June futures at 4295.
In another deal a long cylinder was established by buying 1,000 September 3825 puts at 45p, selling 1,000 September 4725 calls at 36p and buying June futures at 4310.
Profits will be made from the long futures position if the market goes higher, but above 4725 there is a risk of being assigned the short calls.
And if FTSE futures fall below 3825, losses from the futures position can be limited by exercising the puts.

Over in stock options, dealers believed a short position in British Petroleum was rolled forward. It involved buying back 500 April 650 calls at 54p in a closing deal and establishing a new one by selling 500 July 650 calls at 68p.
In insurer Royal & Sun Alliance, there was a buyer of 400 April 460 calls at 7p. The uderlying shares gained 11-1/2p to 450-1/2p while those of BP were up 2-1/2p to 701p.
